info.title: SmartLogistics
info.description:
Every service's API as the gateway exposes it on :8000. Each tag is owned by one service; `x-service` on an operation names it.

Log in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, then authorise with the `access_token`.

post.summary: Hold stock for a shipment (all lines or none)
post.description:
Rows are locked in id order, so concurrent requests for the same units
serialise: the first wins and the second gets `insufficient_stock`. The
hold stays *unconfirmed* until `shipment.created` arrives, and returns the
SKU facts Shipment snapshots onto its items.

200.description: Already held: the existing hold is returned

post.summary: Create a shipment and hold its stock
post.description:
Reserves stock with Inventory first (one synchronous call), then records
the shipment and `shipment.created` in one transaction. With an
`Idempotency-Key`, a retry returns the original response and reuses the
same hold.

row and a `shipment.status_changed` event. Concurrent changes to the same
shipment cannot both apply: the loser gets 409 `concurrent_update`.

ReservationRequest.title: ReservationRequest
ReservationRequest.description:
Hold stock for one shipment. ``shipment_id`` is the idempotency key:
repeating the same request returns the existing hold.

ShipmentCreate.title: ShipmentCreate
ShipmentCreate.description:
Creates a shipment in ``created`` status.

The destination address is supplied inline rather than by id: an address is
a snapshot of where this parcel was sent, and editing a customer's saved
address must never rewrite a delivered shipment's destination.

ShipmentItemCreate.description: A line on a new shipment. SKU attributes are snapshotted server-side.

ShipmentUpdate.title: ShipmentUpdate
ShipmentUpdate.description:
Editable only before dispatch.

Status is absent by design: transitions go through dedicated endpoints so
each can enforce its own rules and side effects.

WeeklyScheduleUpdate.title: WeeklyScheduleUpdate
WeeklyScheduleUpdate.description:
Replaces the whole week at once.

Partial edits of a schedule are ambiguous — an absent day could mean
'unchanged' or 'closed' — so the full week is always supplied.
